title: Route handshake error log and quick hypotheses
content:
Quick scratchpad capturing CLI commands, logs, and hypotheses from the regional routing incident (AZ-1 -> AZ-3 failover attempt) on 2026-03-12. Purpose: preserve breadcrumbs for followup and handoff to SRE oncall.

Summary of what I saw (high-level):
- At ~2026-03-12T14:06:02Z we saw a spike in 5xxs for customer-tenant-42 in eu-west-1. Errors looked like connection handshakes failing when the request was routed to a fallback variant in a different region. Many requests retried and recovered; ~12% of requests observed > 2s extra latency and ~3% got hard 502/504s.
- Smart routing policy v3 had just been rolled out to eu-west-1 (canary 10% -> 100% on 2026-03-11). The policy includes latency-based routing with capacity tiers and a regional-fallback rule when capacity < 0.15.

Commands and checks I ran (ordered, with outputs trimmed to salient lines):

1) Check the route decision logs from the routing service for a representative request-id (req=0af3b6..)
- cmd: curl -s "http://internal-routing-api/admin/decisions?req_id=0af3b6" | jq '.steps'
- excerpted output: "[{\"step\":\"select-pool\",\"pool\":\"eu-west-1-pool\"},{\"step\":\"apply-policy-v3\",\"result\":\"fallback\",\"reason\":\"capacity_breach:0.12<0.15\"},{\"step\":\"route\",\"target\":\"eu-central-1-pool\"}]"
- note: decision shows fallback triggered due to capacity threshold.

2) Inspect capacity metrics at the time from prometheus via query. (I used the short curl to the prometheus read API)
- cmd: curl -s "http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(gpu_utilization[5m])%20by%20(region)%20%3E%200.8"
- quick check: eu-west-1 had a 5m avg GPU utilization of 0.86 across the dedicated pool at 14:05Z. eu-central-1 was lower (~0.45).

3) Routing agent logs on node that made the errant handshake (node id r-agent-eu-west-1-045)
- cmd: ssh r-agent-eu-west-1-045 'sudo journalctl -u route-agent -o short-iso --since "2026-03-12 13:58" --until "2026-03-12 14:12" | grep -i "handshake\|connect\|error" -n'
- relevant lines:
  2026-03-12T14:05:59Z route-agent[1128]: INFO select-pool: eu-west-1-pool score=0.73 capacity=0.12
  2026-03-12T14:06:00Z route-agent[1128]: WARN apply-policy: fallback -> target eu-central-1-pool
  2026-03-12T14:06:01Z route-agent[1128]: ERROR dial tcp 10.8.21.64:9200: connect: connection refused
  2026-03-12T14:06:02Z route-agent[1128]: ERROR handshake failed: EOF (tls: use of closed connection)

- interpretation: agent attempted connect to target pool but connection refused and TLS handshake died with "use of closed connection".

4) Netstat / iptables snapshot on the agent node around time (grabbed quickly via remote command)
- cmd: ssh r-agent-eu-west-1-045 'sudo ss -tnp | grep 9200 || true'
- returned nothing (no established/connected sockets to 10.8.21.64:9200) — consistent with immediate connect errors.

5) Health API of target pool endpoint (eu-central-1 node):
- cmd: curl -s -v http://10.8.21.64:9200/health
- result (first attempt): "* Connection refused"
- second attempt 14:07:03Z: 200 {"status":"ok","replicas":3,"leader":"model-infer-12"}
- observation: short period of connection refusing, then recovered within ~1 minute.

6) Check autoscaler logs for eu-central-1 pool
- cmd: curl -s "http://autoscaler/api/events?pool=eu-central-1-pool&from=2026-03-12T13:50:00Z&to=2026-03-12T14:10:00Z" | jq '.events[] | {ts:.ts, type:.type, detail:.detail}'
- salient items:
  {"ts":"2026-03-12T14:05:55Z","type":"scale-down","detail":"shrink nodes from 4 -> 2 (policy: aggressive)"}
  {"ts":"2026-03-12T14:06:45Z","type":"scale-up","detail":"scale up 2 -> 4 because pending_queue > threshold"}
- interpretation: autoscaler performed aggressive scale-down right before the routing decisions; capacity breaching likely accurate but momentary.

7) KV prefix cache state for customer-tenant-42 on route-agent
- cmd: redis-cli -h redis-routing get route:tenant:42:prefix_cache
- result: "{\"last_sync\":\"2026-03-12T13:59:01Z\",\"pending\":false}"
- no obvious stale cache, but last sync was ~6 minutes before incident.

8) TLS cert check on eu-central node that refused
- cmd: openssl s_client -connect 10.8.21.64:9200 -servername infer-service.example 2>/dev/null | head -n 10
- snippet: "CONNECTED(00000003)\n139936292...\n---\nno peer certificate available\n---\nssl handshake failure: error:1408A0C1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher"
- suggests a brief TLS negotiation mismatch between client and server stacks. How did client get mismatched cipher list? Hard to say.

Error snippets observed across systems:
- "dial tcp 10.8.21.64:9200: connect: connection refused"
- "handshake failed: EOF (tls: use of closed connection)"
- "ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher"
- routing decision message: "capacity_breach:0.12<0.15"
- agent metric emitted: route_attempts=125, route_success=121, route_failures=4

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Autoscaler race + abrupt scale-down: autoscaler removed nodes in eu-central-1 at 14:05:55Z (aggressive policy) and the routing decision layer saw the reduced capacity metric and triggered fallback to eu-central-1 (???). Wait — decision shows fallback TO eu-central-1 because the local pool eu-west-1 breached capacity threshold. So agent tried to route out-of-region to eu-central-1 but a node in eu-central was momentarily not accepting connections (scale-down/scale-up race), creating connection refused and TLS handshake mismatches. Likely transient.
2) Rolling update or config push on eu-central-1 at same time: separate deploy might have restarted service and temporarily changed TLS ciphers (e.g., openssl downgrade or new server config). Check deploy logs. If routing agent attempted handshake during a narrow window while backend was restarting it could see these errors.
3) Networking flap between AZ boundaries (MTU or firewall rule applied) causing connection resets — less likely since kube/host network logs don't show broad packet loss.
4) Bug in route-agent TLS stack: older agent binary presented ciphers not accepted by newer infer-service. But that would be persistent, not transient. Also other regions didn't show this.

Remediation actions I executed (and results):
- Temporarily pinned tenant-42 routing policy to v2 (previous stable) at 14:12Z for 20 minutes to reduce additional cross-region trips while we investigate. Command: curl -X POST http://routing-api/admin/policies/tenant-42 -d '{"policy":"v2","force":true}'
  -> immediate change in routing decisions; error rate for tenant-42 dropped to baseline within ~3m.
- Sent a throttled rolling restart of route-agent on r-agent-eu-west-1-045 and 046 to clear any stuck sockets and force re-sync of TLS contexts. route-agent restarted cleanly, logs show re-sync with redis and updated TLS context at 14:20Z.
- Raised autoscaler policy ticket: autoscaler config for eu-central-1 used aggressive scale-down policy with minimum cushion=0.0; proposed change: set cushion=1 and cooldown=120s to avoid scale-down during traffic spikes. Jira: AUTOSCALE-311.

Data to collect for postmortem (what we still need):
- Full deploy and CI/CD timelines for eu-central-1 at 14:00-14:10 (who deployed what?). Check CD pipeline: github.com/redwood-inference/infer-service/actions/runs
- Full tcpdump from route-agent egress interface at 14:05-14:07 (small capture) — need packet-level proof for 'connection refused' vs RST vs network blackhole.
- Autoscaler decision logs and node termination times for nodes that were removed at 14:05:55Z. Need to confirm whether the node that refused was one of the terminated nodes and whether it exposed an IP briefly during termination.
- TLS cipher lists both client and server as observed by connection attempts at the time. We saw openssl error; need server-side openssl logs.
- Cross-check with telemetry: which tenants saw the issue (only tenant-42 or others)? quick query: sum(rate(requests_total{code=502}[5m])) by (tenant) shows spikes for 42 and 77 concurrently.

Quick notes / scratch of alternative experiments to run:
- Reproduce locally by simulating a scale-down event (terminate a backend instance) while sending continuous requests from route-agent to observe failure modes.
- Temporarily enable more verbose route-agent TLS negotiation logs (debug level) and leave enabled for 30m during next maintenance window.
- Add hysteresis to policy v3: require capacity < 0.12 for 30s before triggering cross-region fallback; or require consecutive 2 samples. This will avoid reactive cross-region trips on short blips.

Draft timeline for Slack message to customer-facing SRE and Product (short):
- 14:05 UTC — transient connection failures observed while routing tenant-42 traffic off-region.
- 14:12 UTC — temporarily pinned to routing policy v2, errors reduced to baseline.
- 14:20 UTC — route-agents restarted, autoscaler policy change proposed (AUTOSCALE-311).
- Next: gather deploy/autoscaler logs and packet capture; create incident postmortem doc when data collected.

Outstanding owners and next steps (who/what/when):
- Priya: collect tcpdump from r-agent-eu-west-1-045 and upload to incident bucket (by 2026-03-14).
- Ethan: fetch CD/CI deploy history for eu-central-1 at 14:00-14:10 and confirm no coincident deploys (by EOD 2026-03-13).
- Samir: pull autoscaler decision logs and annotate node termination timestamps (by 2026-03-13).
- Eng-sre team: propose policy tolerance/hysteresis change for policy v3 (RFC) and schedule rollback window if needed.

Random scratch thoughts / TODOs for later cleaning:
- Consider adding a 'drain handshake' state in autoscaler so nodes gracefully stop accepting new connect attempts but still serve in-flight until route agents re-sync.
- Add automated test that simulates a small-scale cross-region fallback during a scale-down and asserts no 5xxs above 0.5%.
- Check if route-agent uses TLS 1.2-only or supports TLS 1.3; ensure server stack and client stacks overlap.

End of notes. Keep this as a working artifact; will convert to incident write-up after we collect tcpdump and deploy timeline.
